comps.keepReason: Discovery West 2025 sale at $661/sqft, smaller 2725 sqft and 3 baths
comps.publicRemarks: Welcome to Ollin Construction's newest project in Discovery West. This prairie-style home offers the best of mostly main-level living with a generous primary suite, guest suite with full bath, and dedicated study off the well-appointed kitchen with walk-in pantry. Expansive windows in the living and dining areas capture abundant southern light and create a bright, inviting atmosphere. Upstairs features a third bedroom, full bath, and bonus room with closet that could function as a fourth bedroom. Thoughtfully curated finishes include walnut cabinetry, quartz counters, designer tile selections, matte black fixtures, warm brass lighting, and wide plank white oak flooring. Premium Thermador appliances include a 36'' gas range, built-in refrigerator, speed oven, and dual dishwashers. The 3-car garage includes a 26' deep bay with an 11' door-ideal for a Sprinter van or all your Central Oregon toys. Exceptional floor plans, elevated finishes, and attention to detail define Ollin Construction.

If you're looking for modern design without sacrificing warmth, this Discovery West home deserves a closer look. Designed by Likens Interior Design, it offers clean, contemporary finishes, abundant natural light, and an easy main level layout. One of its standout features is the oversized, fenced back yard with plenty of room to entertain, garden, or play. The kitchen is equally notable, with abundant cabinetry, a walk-in pantry, and windows overlooking the backyard. The primary suite is tucked privately at the back of the home, while two front bedrooms and a full bath provide flexibility for guests, a home office, or both. The dining area feels connected to the living space while maintaining its own identity, framed by oversized windows that bring the outdoors in. Upstairs, a spacious bonus room, private bedroom and bath, plus generous storage offer even more flexibility. Trails, parks, westside shopping and dining, and highly rated schools are all close by.

Set on an oversized rim lot in Discovery West, this Prairie-style home by MCD Homes blends clean lines with elevated detail. Inside, 10-foot ceilings and expansive windows frame rim views, filling the open living and dining spaces with natural light. At the heart of the home is a chef's kitchen with Thermador appliances and an oversized butler's pantry, ideal for everyday living and entertaining. The main-level primary suite offers privacy and backyard views, creating a true retreat. Upstairs, 3 beds, 2 baths, and a bonus space add flexibility. The interior design reflects elevated Northwest modern style—warm, restrained, and intentionally timeless. Natural stone, soft wood tones, and layered textures create a calm, refined environment. With a 3-car garage and thoughtful floor plan, there's room for toys, work, and play. Outside, the expansive backyard stretches toward the rim, offering space to gather or enjoy the Bend lifestyle with trails, parks, and dining just beyond your door.

Beautifully crafted farmhouse by MCD Homes on a premier corner lot in Discovery West, offering added elbow room and timeless curb appeal. Classic farmhouse architecture is elevated with thoughtfully integrated modern features throughout. Soaring 10-foot ceilings and warm wood floors enhance the main level, creating an inviting yet refined atmosphere. The chef's kitchen showcases Thermador appliances, expansive stone surfaces, and floor-to-ceiling cabinetry, blending everyday function with elevated design. From the detailed powder bath to the spa-inspired primary suite with layered textures and curated tilework, every space reflects MCD's signature quiet luxury - understated, intentional, and impeccably executed. Upstairs offers three bedrooms, a beautifully finished bath, and a spacious bonus room. A main-level office, 3-car garage, and coveted RV garage provide flexibility for work and recreation. Generous outdoor living completes this exceptional Discovery West home.

comps.publicRemarks: Experience exceptional westside living in Discovery West with this stunning mid-century modern home by Structure Development NW, featured on the 2026 COBA Tour of Homes. Backing to Discovery Park with beautiful views, this 3,253 SqFt residence offers 4 bedrooms, 3.5 baths, and a thoughtfully designed layout with both the luxurious primary suite and guest suite on the main level. The primary retreat features a soaking tub, radiant heated floors, and a spacious walk-in closet. An open floor plan, upscale finishes, and a gas fireplace create a warm yet refined great room setting. Upstairs, enjoy a large bonus room, two additional bedrooms, and a full bath. Complete with a mud room, laundry room, covered back patio, fully landscaped yard, and an expansive 3-car garage with a Sprinter van bay, this home blends style, comfort, and function. Conveniently located near schools, trails, parks and dining.

comps.publicRemarks: Brand New Quality Construction in the latest phase of popular Discovery West in NW Bend. Walk or bike out your door to trails, shops, restaurants, schools and parks. This mid century modern, single level home sits on a .21/acre lot, next to the community path, giving it extra space between the homes. This builder is known for being ''hands on'', overseeing every detail of the home, he is available to buyers not just during the sale process, but in the years to come. This is an ideal home and neighborhood for the Bend lifestyle.

tenures.detail: Oregon runs every residential tenancy of a dwelling unit through one statute, the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act at ORS chapter 90, and it applies the same way in every city and county. You set the starting rent freely. The increase rules take over once the tenancy begins: nothing during the first year, then one increase per 12-month period on 90 days written notice, capped at the percentage the state publishes for that calendar year. The 2026 figure is 9.5% for an ordinary residential tenancy, which is the lesser of 10 percent or 7 percent plus the September 12-month average change in the West Region consumer price index. A different ceiling of 6% governs space rent in a manufactured-home facility or marina with more than 30 spaces, which runs under ORS 90.600 instead. A unit whose first certificate of occupancy issued less than 15 years before the notice is exempt from the cap entirely, as is a unit regulated or certified as affordable housing. Terminations follow the same first-year line: 30 days written notice with no reason given during the first year of occupancy, and after that only for a tenant cause or a qualifying landlord reason such as moving in, selling to a buyer who will occupy, demolition, conversion, or repairs that require the unit to be vacant. Oregon also bars cities and counties from adopting their own rent control, so the state ceiling is the ceiling at this address.
tenures.citation: ORS 90.323 and 90.324 (rent increases), ORS 90.427 (terminations), ORS 90.320 (habitability), ORS 90.300 (deposits), ORS 659A.421 (source of income), ORS 91.225 (no local rent control). 2026 maximum 9.5% for a residential tenancy and 6% for facility space rent (ORS 90.600), per Oregon Department of Administrative Services, 2026 rent stabilization percentages (correction published 2025-10-01), calculated under ORS 90.324(1).
tenures.headline: Yes. A 12-month lease is available here, and one statewide rulebook governs it.
requirements: Keep the rent-increase clock. No increase during the first year of the tenancy. After that, one increase per 12-month period, 90 days written notice, and no more than the maximum the state publishes for that calendar year. The 2026 maximum is 9.5% for an ordinary residential tenancy, and 6% for space rent in a manufactured-home facility or marina with more than 30 spaces. ORS 90.323(2), ORS 90.324(1), ORS 90.600.

Maintain the unit in habitable condition for the whole tenancy: weatherproofing, working plumbing, hot and cold running water, heat, safe wiring, working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and working locks on entry doors and windows. ORS 90.320(1).
Return the security deposit with a written accounting within 31 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant delivers possession. ORS 90.300(12) and (13).
Screen without regard to source of income. Oregon counts federal rent subsidy under 42 U.S.C. 1437f and any other local, state or federal housing assistance as protected. ORS 659A.421.

Plan terminations around the first-year line. During the first year of occupancy a month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days written notice with no reason given. After the first year it ends only for a tenant cause or a qualifying landlord reason, on 90 days written notice, with one month periodic rent in relocation assistance unless you hold an ownership interest in four or fewer residential dwelling units. ORS 90.427(3), (5) and (6).
Give the 30 days written notice before the end date of a fixed term that expires inside the first year of occupancy. Without it the tenancy carries on. ORS 90.427(4)(b).
Tell your insurer the unit is tenant occupied. An owner-occupied homeowner policy is not a landlord policy.
Read the recorded CC&Rs and any association rules before you count on a 12-month lease. An association can set a minimum lease term, a rental cap, or a registration step that the code does not.

Deschutes County adds nothing to the state rulebook for a long-term tenancy. County Title 5 carries no rental registration or inspection program, and the only county rental registration is the transient lodging Certificate of Authority under DCC 4.08.140, which reaches short-term rentals only.

tenures.detail: Oregon has no separate mid-term category, so two independent lines decide what a stay is, and both point the same way for a 30-day-plus program. Deschutes County ties its short-term rental rules to occupancy, which DCC 4.08.050 defines as use for less than 30 consecutive calendar days. DCC 4.08.052 goes further and says a person who pays for lodging on a monthly basis, regardless of the number of days in the month, is not an occupant at all. A stay of 30 days or longer, or any tenancy billed monthly, sits outside county short-term rental registration and outside the county room tax. That matters most on farm and forest land, where the county prohibits short-term rentals and leaves 30-day-plus and long-term rental open. Oregon draws the same line for lodging tax: a guest who stays 30 or more consecutive days at the same facility is exempt, and the exemption covers the entire stay. The second line is the tenancy line, and it is the one that catches people. A stay escapes ORS chapter 90 only as a vacation occupancy, and that takes all three of these at once: the occupant rents for vacation purposes only and not as a principal residence, the occupant has a principal residence somewhere other than this unit, and the authorized period of occupancy does not exceed 45 days. Miss any one of the three and the occupant is a tenant with habitability, deposit accounting, and written termination notice attached from the first day. A 13-week travel contract that makes this address the occupant's residence creates a tenancy. It is not a vacation stay. The other exclusion, transient occupancy, does not reach a house: it requires daily charging, daily or every-other-day maid and linen service, and it is excluded only in a hotel or motel. The practical read for this property: a furnished 30-day-plus rental avoids the short-term rental permit and the room tax, and in exchange it is a tenancy, so write it as a fixed term and run it under ORS chapter 90 from day one.
tenures.citation: ORS 90.100 (definitions of vacation occupancy and transient occupancy), ORS 90.110(4) and (6) (exclusions), ORS 90.427(4)(b) (fixed term ending in the first year), ORS 320.300(11) and ORS 320.308(6) (state lodging tax definition and the 30-consecutive-day exemption). Local: Deschutes County Code 4.08.050 and 4.08.052 (occupancy and occupant, Ord. 2025-006, effective 2025-09-01).
tenures.headline: Open, and it is the widest path here. A stay of 30 days or longer is not a short-term rental.
requirements: Decide which of the two the stay is before anyone signs. Vacation occupancy takes all three tests in ORS 90.100. Anything else is a tenancy under ORS chapter 90 no matter how short it is.

Write a fixed term. A fixed term whose ending date falls inside the first year of occupancy ends without cause on 30 days written notice given before that date. Skip the notice and the tenancy carries on. ORS 90.427(4)(b).

Charge by the month rather than by the day. Daily charging plus daily or every-other-day maid and linen service is the transient-occupancy pattern in ORS 90.100, and that exclusion only applies in a hotel or motel.
Meet the habitability standard and the 31-day deposit accounting even on a 60-day stay. ORS 90.320 and ORS 90.300 do not have a length floor.
Inventory the furnishings in the agreement and price the turnover. A furnished mid-term unit refills several times a year, and each refill carries a cleaning, a listing, and a vacancy gap.

Confirm the lodging-tax exemption with the taxing office in writing before you stop collecting on a long stay. Oregon exempts a dwelling unit occupied by the same person for a consecutive period of 30 days or more, and the exemption covers the whole stay. ORS 320.308(6). Local room tax runs on its own ordinance.

tenures.detail: We could not resolve a zone-level short-term rental read for this parcel, so we are not going to state one. Nightly rental in Oregon is regulated locally: the city or county decides whether the zone allows it, whether a land use permit or a license is required, and what room tax attaches. The operating steps below apply wherever nightly rental is allowed.
tenures.citation: Short-term rental regulation is local. Confirm with the permitting jurisdiction for this address.
tenures.headline: Confirm nightly rental with the office that permits it for this address.
requirements: Confirm the zone of record and the short-term rental status with Deschutes County Community Development and the Deschutes County Tax Office before you plan on nightly income. We are not going to state a permit answer we could not resolve from the record.
Confirm the local room tax rate, the registration deadline, and who remits it with the same office.
Register with the Oregon Department of Revenue for the 1.5% state transient lodging tax if nightly rental turns out to be available. ORS 320.305(1)(a).
Read the recorded CC&Rs and any association rules in parallel. A private covenant can restrict nightly rental independently of the city or county code.
Long-term leasing and stays of 30 days or longer do not depend on that answer. Both are available at this address today.

rental.disclaimer: We read each of these rules at its primary source on 2026-07-30, and every answer cites the statute or code section we relied on. Rental law in Oregon changes every legislative session, the state republishes the maximum rent increase every September, and a recorded covenant or an association rule can be stricter than the code. None of this is legal advice, tax advice, or a land-use decision. Verify anything you plan to rely on with the office that issues it, and with your own attorney and CPA, before you buy on the strength of it.
rental.economicsNote: Three tenures, three different engines, and they do not price the same way. A long-term lease trades the top of the market for occupancy: one rent, twelve months or more, one turnover, and an increase ceiling set by the state each year. A mid-term stay of 30 days or longer carries no room tax and no short-term rental permit, and pays for that in furnishings, more frequent turnover, and vacancy between stays. A nightly rental prices by the night and pays for it in room tax, cleaning, linens, management, platform fees, licensing, and a season that is not flat across the year. What decides the number in every case is the same short list: the rate the unit actually achieves, how many nights or months it is occupied, and the operating cost stack underneath. We do not publish a nightly rate, an occupancy percentage, a cap rate, or a yield for this address, because no source we can cite carries those figures for this property, and a number we cannot trace is worse than no number. To model it with real inputs, get four things: a written rent opinion from a Central Oregon property manager for the long-term figure, a revenue history from a short-term rental manager for permitted comparable properties near this one, the association rules and dues if the property is in one, and an insurance quote for the use you intend.

marketingHighlights.basis: Deschutes County Code 4.08.050 defines taxable occupancy as use for less than 30 consecutive calendar days. State exemption per ORS 320.308(6). The stay runs as a tenancy under ORS chapter 90.
marketingHighlights.headline: A stay of 30 days or longer is not a short-term rental. No nightly permit, no local room tax, and the state exempts the whole stay at 30 consecutive days.

marketingHighlights.basis: ORS 91.225 (state preemption of local rent control), with the annual ceiling set by ORS 90.324(1).
marketingHighlights.headline: Long-term leasing here runs on one statewide rulebook. Oregon bars cities and counties from layering their own rent control on top.

subject.publicRemarks: Truly an incredible value! Single-level, mid-century modern stunner in Discovery West built by BendTrend Homes. The home was designed to seamlessly blend nature, quality, and accessibility in a functional and sophisticated space. The vaulted plan sprawls 3,172 sf and boasts 4 beds, 4 baths, a den and 3-car garage with an RV/sprinter bay w/11 ft door. This home shines with its rich and refined materials that complement our high desert surroundings such as custom walnut cabinets, white oak floors, matte black fixtures, quartz counters and brick fireplace. You'll enjoy radiant heat in a spa-like primary bath, AC to cool the warm days and a private patio equipped for your fire pit, BBQ and hot tub. Glass sliders open over the Discovery Park trail system which, in moments, will have you biking on Phil's Trail, sipping coffee at Discovery Corner or letting your pups play off-leash at the park. Live easy in this beautifully crafted home accessible to so much of why we love to call Bend home!
